_what: THE ELECTRONICS' ROUTE in this rack — this piece's USE of the engine's sound seam (electronics/docs/SEAMS.md). Which instrument track stands for which player's microphone, and the one flat track the engine's master returns on. Read by tools/elec.js; put into the rack through the bridge (reaper/bridge/jobs/elec_route.lua). Channels are ReaRoute's, counted from 1 as Reaper names them.
_made: 2026-10-04, PLAN 1.1 · 6.1 (RUNNING_LOG §51): one player for the first proof. 2026-10-05 (RUNNING_LOG §71, impulse 1): the other four — the percussion's microphone is the shime daiko's track for now (one track per player row; the other seven percussion tracks get a send as the music uses them). engineIn 3 is the latency loop.
_message: THE MESSAGE ROUTE (PLAN 1.1 · 6.2; RUNNING_LOG §60): where the score server sends the page's messages — the engine's LANGUAGE port, UDP 57211 (its server is 57210). In concert and in simulation the same road; this address is the one thing that may differ. testOnsets: A ROUTE CHECK, off since the mic opening is a brick of its own (6.3, RUNNING_LOG §64) — the hook that sent it is out of the composer page; the engine still shows an /le/onset a tool sends. Read at every request: no restart needed.
_bank: THE BANK (PLAN 1.1 · 6.3 … 6.5; RUNNING_LOG §64): dir = where the engine keeps this piece's samples — <dir>/<name>.wav the cropped samples (COMMITTED: the samples are the piece's), <dir>/raw/ the whole recordings (gitignored, kept for a re-crop), <dir>/index.json a row per sample (the engine writes it; the composer page reads it at /bank/samples/index.json). crop = THE CROP'S RULE where this piece overrides the engine's defaults (electronics/sc/bank.scd): attackDb -30 · floorDb -50 · preMs 5 · endDb -45 · holdMs 50 · fadeInMs 2 · fadeOutMs 10 — HIS EAR TUNES THEM; a number written here is used from the engine's next start. Both are given to the engine at its START (tools/elec.js start), never by a message.
_listenEcho: A ROUTE CHECK (RUNNING_LOG §55): above 0, `start` returns each note this many seconds LATER, so the route is heard as a second sound. 0 since the playback brick exists (6.5, RUNNING_LOG §64): the engine returns what it MAKES — a sample played back — and nothing of the player's own sound.
_mode: THE MODE (RUNNING_LOG §71, 2026-10-05; his design): one word that names which bank FILLS the engine's buffers at start, where captures are WRITTEN, and whether an opening records. compose = bank/samples both ways, openings record (the latest take wins) · compose-locked = the same samples, openings change nothing · rehearsal = the players record the BACKUP bank (bank/backup) · concert = buffers full from the backup, a live capture replaces one only when it caught a sound, the captures kept in bank/live/<date>. The bricks in the score are the same in every mode. Read at the engine's START (tools/elec.js start).
